centered-guides.json.title: MakeICT Ultimaker 2 retrofit
centered-guides.json.target: Replace the integrated printer motion board with Prime P12 motor-phase outputs. Use the depicted XT30 J12 VFET power entry and qualified heater, fan and temperature circuits; the optional RTD interface is firmware-gated.
centered-guides.json.plan: Original motion-driver electronics are on the board being replaced. Use Prime integrated phase outputs directly to measured winding pairs; do not connect STEP/DIR signal outputs to motor windings. Confirm installed board, motor current and power rating from the cited machine source. Selected architecture: Prime P12 with integrated motor drivers. The main diagram and connection-ID schedule define the current proposed routes. Dotted function-coloured GUESS routes need the named commissioning checks; OPEN routes remain disconnected until the missing terminal, rating or interface is established. Previous Core alternatives remain only in the superseded historical architecture record.

GUESS

Analog Devices MAX31865PMB1 data sheet Rev 0 (Jan 2014), Table 1: all 12-pin J1 positions: 1=SS/CS, 2=MOSI, 3=MISO, 4=SCLK, 5 and 11=GND, 6 and 12=+3.3V, 7=DRDY active-low, 8–10=NC. Installed BOM R7 is 400Ω ±0.1% RREF for the board PT100 configuration. The MAX31865 BIAS node is internal to the module (not a user terminal). CON1.1=FORCE+/FORCE2, .2=RTDIN+, .3=RTDIN−, .4=FORCE−. Install both J2 jumpers 1–2 and 3–4 for 2-wire RTD; connect the two sensor leads to CON1.1 and CON1.4. J1.6 is the proposed board supply contact; J1.5 is GND. Prime J36 SPI signal contacts are source-derived, but PD15 CS is only a candidate. Smoothieware docs state MAX31865 is a future possibility, not an existing temperature-control driver, so this circuit remains unusable for closed-loop heater control until firmware support and the board 3.3V output are verified. R7 and BIAS are factory-internal details noted here, not external user wiring terminals. The diagram shows every J2 pin separately with two physical jumpers; no invented J2-to-screw-terminal cable is required.

Board-side evidence: exact P12 schematic/PCB at commit7dc4f9a identifies J17 Hotend A, J18 Hotend B, J19 Fan1, J20 Fan2. J17.1 receives shared Q25 cutoff-controlled VFET; J17.2 is Q19 switched return. These are factory internal circuits, not user soldering instructions. PE0 / HOTEND_A_FET and PF14 / OUTPUTENABLE come from the exact P12 source; a general documentation PJ6 label conflicts and must not override this revision. Heater/sensor fitment and connector-safe current are unknown: measure, qualify firmware and prove thermal shutdown before connecting heat. No guaranteed 5A terminal rating is asserted.

wire_panels.note: Analog Devices MAX31865PMB1 data sheet Rev 0 (Jan 2014), Table 1: all 12-pin J1 positions: 1=SS/CS, 2=MOSI, 3=MISO, 4=SCLK, 5 and 11=GND, 6 and 12=+3.3V, 7=DRDY active-low, 8–10=NC. Installed BOM R7 is 400Ω ±0.1% RREF for the board PT100 configuration. The MAX31865 BIAS node is internal to the module (not a user terminal). CON1.1=FORCE+/FORCE2, .2=RTDIN+, .3=RTDIN−, .4=FORCE−. Install both J2 jumpers 1–2 and 3–4 for 2-wire RTD; connect the two sensor leads to CON1.1 and CON1.4. J1.6 is the proposed board supply contact; J1.5 is GND. Prime J36 SPI signal contacts are source-derived, but PD15 CS is only a candidate. Smoothieware docs state MAX31865 is a future possibility, not an existing temperature-control driver, so this circuit remains unusable for closed-loop heater control until firmware support and the board 3.3V output are verified. R7 and BIAS are factory-internal details noted here, not external user wiring terminals. The diagram shows every J2 pin separately with two physical jumpers; no invented J2-to-screw-terminal cable is required. Pinned P12 PCB pad readback verifies J35.1 /3V3_LIMIT and J35.10 GND; available current and fitted revision remain qualification gates.
